$comment: Repository-level workflow configuration. `branches.base` is the integration branch every issue PR targets and `bun run land` merges into; `branches.release` is the production branch `bun run release` fast-forwards after the full health gate passes on the base tip (ADR 0116). `branches.*` is read by scripts/lib/branches.ts and, via jq, by .claude/hooks/deny-guard.sh and scripts/gate-run.sh — no script or hook names a branch by literal. `landRunner.*` is the land-runner (issue #5469), read by scripts/lib/land-runner.ts ONLY: `platform` is the `process.platform` of the ONE machine that merges (topology B', ADR 0154: the MacBook, `darwin`; the Huawei never runs it — `land:runner` exits on any other platform), `intervalS` the seconds between ticks of a quiet queue. `TOLARIA_LAND_RUNNER_PLATFORM` overrides `landRunner.platform` for one process (empty = runs nowhere; issue #5590). `afkDispatch.*` is the AFK dispatcher's (issue #5957), parsed by scripts/lib/afk-dispatch.ts ONLY (scripts/afk-dispatch.ts hands it the file): `repairAgeHours` is how long a repair pick (an open PR labelled `land-failed`) may wait while the dispatcher HOLDS before a run fails once, so GitHub emails the owner — a hold exits 0, and on 2026-10-18 six such PRs waited 3–20 h under `no-pass-workflow` with no signal; 4 h is a fraction of that wait and above a land-runner retry's minutes. `queueMax` and `failedMax` are its admission by queue depth (issue #6988): no NEW pick while open `ready-to-land` PRs number `queueMax` or more (resumes and repairs still run), repairs only while open `land-failed` PRs number `failedMax` or more — measured on 2026-10-24 → 10-25, when 127 passes met 70 merges (2.9/h) and the queue grew without bound: 6 is two hours of merges at 2.9/h, 4 is the `land-failed` count past which the queue is broken rather than slow (18:55Z that day: 24, 16 of them with nothing wrong, issue #6957, issue #6986). `laneBotBudget.*` is the scoped lanes' bot test admission (issue #6943, ADR 0154 §13), read by scripts/lib/bot-test-costs.ts ONLY: a reached `*.bot.test.ts` file runs in an `engine`, `skin` or `cards` lane when its measured cost (data/bot-test-costs.json, `bun run bot:costs`: the median of its wall over the newest `medianOfRuns` health runs) is at most `perFileS`, cheapest first, until the admitted files sum to `totalS` — the ~10 s guard budget of issue #4963; the rest is named in a skip line with its cost. `admission.*` is the bar an Admission Candidate clears (issue #3985, GLOSSARY.md § Admission), read by `verdicts:promote` ONLY (scripts/lib/verdict-promotion-run.ts hands it to convex/gre/ai/verdicts/admission.ts): `minPersons` (distinct people who attested it explicitly, aliased accounts one person), `ownerPersons` (authors `${deployment}:${userId}` whose person's attestation alone suffices — here the owner's production account, aliased to their dev one in the Verdict Store), `minConsecutivePromotions` (Promotions in a row the Weight Fit kept it satisfied, read off data/verdicts.streaks.json), `seeds` and `iterations` (the whole-Bot pick check: an allowed move on EVERY seed at that fixed budget — `iterations` is the shipped search budget, DEFAULT_BUDGET). Tooling only proposes; the forced-loss check and the Admission stay a human's. `verdictProposals.*` is the Verdict Proposal capture and sampling (issue #3984, GLOSSARY.md § Verdict Proposal), read by src/lib/ai/verdict-proposal-config.ts ONLY: `captureLimit` (human-seat decisions one vs-Bot game keeps, a reservoir, so a long game is sampled evenly rather than truncated), `perClassQuota` (decisions per Decision Class the Brain is consulted on at game end, so per-class proposals never exceed it), `agreeingPerClass` (of those, how many where the Brain AGREED with the player still become proposals — the share that lets the corpus see what the Brain already gets right; at most `perClassQuota`), `iterations` and `seed` (the game-end consult's fixed search budget and seed, the blade's discipline — `iterations` is the shipped budget, DEFAULT_BUDGET). `repairWatch.*` is the stalled-repair alert (issue #7142), read by scripts/lib/repair-watch.ts ONLY: `stallMinutes` is how long a RED may stand with none of its declared repairs merged before `repair:watch` notifies the owner — 30 is a repair's lane on the MacBook (minutes) plus two of pr-gate's 15-minute re-gate sweeps; on 2026-10-27 the revert PR #7136 waited 2 h 39 min unnoticed.
